A volume-scaled distance would fit the evidence better, but most reports carry no volume. shore_m: a lake edge within this of land is shore; gap_km: a run of edges away from land longer than this ends the walk (a state or international line, the edge of the record); shorter runs (a river mouth, a breakwall) are walked across; a record of several polygons is dissolved first, so an NHD tile seam is never an end. snap_km: an outfall farther than this from the shore gets no stretch. oceans (Florida's go-live gates, 2026-11-04): a record of kind bay, sound, sea, ocean, lake or reservoir whose wikidata or name (exactly, normalised) an ocean entry gives is a shoreline water too (shoreline_entry returns the entry with ocean true): openboatlaunch keeps atlantic-ocean-fl and gulf-of-america-fl as bays and north-atlantic-ocean-fl as a sound. Its stretch is walked on the state's coastal waters near the point (build/reaches.py ocean_outline), never on the record's own outline; ocean_open_m 1000: the waters are eroded and grown back by that much, which closes an inlet or pass under 2 km wide (Florida's inlets are about 0.2 to 1 km), and only the pieces that reach the state's offshore line are kept. A bay or sound whose mouth is wider than the opening closes is part of that water and the walk follows its shore (the review of 2026-11-04 walked 13 real points: Mexico Beach into St. Joseph Bay, Clearwater Beach and New Port Richey into St. Joseph Sound, Miami-Dade Central District round Key Biscayne into Biscayne Bay); build/reaches.py ocean_waters_along then adds to the stretch's waters every bay, sound or lake record of the state that 1 km or more of the stretch runs in or within 150 m of (a reach belongs to every water it runs through), found only where the record's outline is here. each_way_km stays 20 for the ocean too: Feddersen et al. (2021) give about 20 km of wave-driven alongshore transport of untreated wastewater on an open sandy coast (Zimmer-Faust et al. 2021) and 8 to 14 km a day; no Florida-specific alongshore measurement was found. Pacific Ocean (California's go-live gates, 2026-11-06): openboatlaunch keeps pacific-ocean-ca as a bay with no wikidata (matched by name, as Florida's), the only CA record of that name; NHD has no CA ocean record; the Feddersen et al. evidence is from the San Diego-Tijuana coast itself; CA's TIGER/Line polygon runs 3 nautical miles out and round the Channel Islands; the Golden Gate (about 1.6 km at its narrowest, 1.7 km on the Census outlines), the San Diego Bay and Humboldt Bay entrances are under 2 km and are closed by the opening (walked on the real files in the review of 2026-11-06: the Golden Gate is closed since that review's fix; San Diego Bay and Humboldt Bay lie inside the land of the 1:500,000 outlines, so the walk passes their mouths in any case), so an ocean stretch does not turn into those bays; Monterey Bay and Santa Monica Bay are open coast. lakes kinds (2026-11-06): a lake entry may list the record kinds it matches (default lake and reservoir) and the states it is applied in; San Francisco Bay (openboatlaunch san-francisco-bay-ca, kind bay, 149,773 acres, wikidata Q232264) is a lake entry with kinds ["bay"] and states ["CA"]: walked on its own outline like Lake St. Clair, worded as a bay (export/build.py BAY_LABEL, status basis "the bay is not coloured whole"). Its record is not cut into named parts: openboatlaunch has no San Pablo Bay, Suisun Bay or South Bay record; the site holds San Pablo Bay, Suisun Bay and Richardson Bay as Census TIGER/Line records with GNIS (2026-11-06), and a bay stretch that runs along one of them lists it among its waters (build/reaches.py shoreline_record, CA final audit 2026-11-06: the Sausalito-Marin City and Paradise Cove stretches along Richardson Bay, West County's along San Pablo Bay) (Carquinez Strait, San Leandro Bay, Islais Creek Channel, the Oakland Estuary and two small East Bay and West Bay pieces are separate records and keep their bay handling). open_m 1000 on its entry (review of 2026-11-06): the hourly run walks the bay on openboatlaunch's outline (restored from R2); without it, on its Census water (census_lake_outline: the TIGER/Line polygon less the land in the record's box grown by 0.05 degrees), which runs out through the Golden Gate onto the Pacific coast; build/reaches.py cut_at_mouths takes away the eroded pieces (by open_m) that lie mostly outside the record's own box, grown back, so a stretch from the Marina crosses the mouth to the Marin shore instead of running down Ocean Beach. The opening of the ocean waters keeps only the eroded pieces near the offshore line before growing them back (review of 2026-11-06: grown back on either side of the Golden Gate, which is narrow only over a short length, the sea and the bay joined again). ocean_tie_offshore_km 22.2 (12 nautical miles, the territorial sea; California's go-live gates, 2026-11-06): a registry outfall whose receiving water is an ocean record is tied to it when EPA's (or the permit's) point lies in open water off the state's shore up to this far out, not only within snap_km: the deep ocean outfalls end 6 to 8 km out (from the state's 1:500,000 outline: Point Loma 7.3 km and San Francisco's Southwest Ocean Outfall 6.5 km at EPA's points, Hyperion's 5-mile outfall 8.0 km and Orange County's 120-inch outfall 7.6 km at their permits' points; review of 2026-11-06); such a point gets no stretch (snap_km) and its reports are listed on the ocean without one. A point inland of the shore is still held beyond snap_km. states ["FL"] on the Atlantic and Gulf entries: applied in Florida first; the live ocean records of Virginia (atlantic-ocean-va), Massachusetts and Maine (north-atlantic-ocean-ma, -me) keep their bay handling until the change is reviewed for them (listing them here would draw their stretches on the next run).

placement.doc: How a report is linked to a water when it does not say exactly where the sewage went.
placement.no_outfall_all_waters_basis: When a combined sewer overflow report does not say which outfall discharged, we show it on every water that the operator's permitted outfalls discharge to, because any of them could have been affected.
placement._no_outfall_all_waters_status: Site default of 2026-11-03, pending the owner's confirmation (docs/decisions.md).

text_over_flag.rationale: Some notices say in their description that sewage entered, may have entered or flowed into a named water, while the notice's form answers that no water body was affected. We follow the description, to err on the side of safety: the report is shown on the water its description names, as a caution and never as an advisory, while the discharge is reported as in progress or ongoing (for up to 7 days with no end), and then for our usual caution period after a reported end. A description that says the sewage did not reach the water, or stayed in a drain or on land, keeps the form's answer. The record shows both the form's answer and the description's words.
text_over_flag.source: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Public Notice of Pollution: each notice's description and its "Waterbodies Impacted" answer.
text_over_flag._doc: build/status.py text_over_flag (rule text_caution, rule_applied placement.text_over_flag); ingest/fl_dep_pnp.py text_reached. Owner, 2026-11-04: the text wins over the form's N, with a note. The site's wording reads this entry (site/src/lib/data.ts textCaution); a source listed here shows the rule on /methods once one of its states is live.

rain_likely.doc: Combined sewers can overflow when it rains hard, and a notice can arrive hours or days after a discharge begins, or not at all. When radar shows that the rain of the last 24 hours at any outfall of a combined sewer system has reached the amount set for that system, and its operator has not reported a discharge that began in the last 24 hours, we show the waters below its outfalls in yellow. Where the amount is the one at which that system has discharged before, from its own reports, or a rain rule its operator or its state publishes, the caution reads "Discharge likely: heavy rain, no report received". Where none exists and our default of 0.1 inch applies, it reads "Discharge possible: heavy rain, no report received", because at that amount many rainy days pass with no overflow. Radar measures the rain at the outfalls, which can differ from the rain over the whole area the sewer drains. A reported discharge or an official advisory takes precedence over this rain caution. This is our caution, based on rainfall (not a report or finding).
rain_likely.label: Discharge likely: heavy rain, no report received

label_by_basis.operator: Discharge likely: heavy rain, no report received
label_by_basis.state: Discharge likely: heavy rain, no report received
label_by_basis.default: Discharge possible: heavy rain, no report received

rain_likely.label_by_basis_rationale: The label says how strong the estimate is. It reads "discharge likely" where the amount comes from the operator's own discharge history or from a rain trigger its state publishes, and "discharge possible" where only our default of 0.1 inch applies. The colour, the rule and how long the caution lasts are the same.

history.doc: Where an operator has enough dated overflow reports, we pair every storm at its outfalls since 2015 with the operator's own reports. The caution reads discharge possible from the smallest storm after which the operator ever reported an overflow, rounded down to the next step, and discharge likely from the smallest step at which it reported an overflow after at least half of the storms of that size and of all larger storms together. Below the possible amount no caution shows only where at least 30 storms that small are on record over at least three years and none was followed by a reported overflow; otherwise the caution starts where a published rule or our default would start it, and lasts at least as long. A reported discharge or an official advisory takes precedence over this rain caution.
history.source: The operators' own dated combined sewer overflow reports, as the operators and state agencies publish them in the sources this site reads; NOAA MRMS daily rainfall totals at each operator's outfalls, from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet reanalysis point service, from 2015.

label_by_level.likely: Discharge likely: heavy rain, no report received
label_by_level.possible: Discharge possible: heavy rain, no report received

history.label_by_level_rationale: With an operator's own record the label follows the storm: "discharge likely" when the rain of the last 24 hours reaches the amount after which the operator reported an overflow after at least half of the storms, and "discharge possible" below it. A water reads "discharge likely" when any of its operators' cautions does.
history.rungs_in_rationale: The steps every amount is rounded down to, in inches of rain in a day, so an amount is never read more finely than the record supports.
history.likely_share_rationale: The caution reads discharge likely from the step at which an overflow was reported after at least half of the storms of that size and larger, the cautious choice.
history.quiet_min_storms_rationale: No caution shows below the smallest storm followed by a reported overflow only when at least 30 storms that small are on record, over at least three years, and none was followed by one.
history.quiet_min_period_days_rationale: Three years of record are needed before small storms can be read as quiet: one or two years of reports cannot show how a system behaves across wet and dry seasons.
history.min_storms_rationale: A size of storm needs at least 10 storms on record before it can set the discharge likely amount; thinner sizes are pooled with their neighbours.
history.min_report_storms_rationale: An operator's record is used only when at least 10 storms were followed by a reported overflow.
history.min_total_storms_rationale: An operator's record is used only when it holds at least 20 storms.
history.min_period_days_rationale: An operator's record is used only when it covers at least a year, so every season is in it.
history._system_changes_doc: A completed project that changed how often a system overflows (a tunnel, a storage basin, sewer separation), cited by its source: {"<permit>": [{"from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "what": "plain words", "source": "citation"}]}. The record for that operator then starts on that day. Until one is cited, a drop in reporting is stated and the whole record is kept.

rain_likely.threshold_rationale: The amount is the 10th percentile of the rainfall on the days the operator discharged: nine discharge days in ten had more rain. It is computed for each operator with at least 10 such days. In Massachusetts it is the rainfall the operator itself reported in its sewage notification reports since July 2022. In Michigan, whose discharge list gives the operator's rainfall for the whole event rather than for one day, it is the NOAA MRMS radar's daily rainfall at the operator's outfalls on the days its reported combined sewer and retention basin discharges began since 2015, the larger of that day's total and the day before's. Operators without that history use a published rule below.
rain_likely.threshold_source: MassDEP Sewage Notification Data System, via the EEA Data Portal (Verified Data Reports, rainfall reported by each permittee); Michigan EGLE, MiEnviro CSO/SSO List, with NOAA MRMS daily rainfall via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet
rain_likely.compare: The NOAA MRMS radar-only rainfall estimate for the 24 hours to the latest hour, read every hour at each outfall from the radar grid. NOAA's radar rainfall service labels its values as inches but has been publishing millimetres; since November 7, 2026 this site works out the unit from the values themselves and from nearby airport rain gauges, converts to inches, and records with each reading the unit it read.
rain_likely.tail_rationale: The caution lasts 48 hours after the 24-hour rainfall total falls back below the amount, as Massachusetts advises avoiding contact during rainstorms and for 48 hours after they end.
rain_likely.notice_suppress_rationale: A discharge notice from the operator that began in the last 24 hours takes over: the waters it names follow the advisory rules above.

default.basis: Our default: 0.1 inch of rain in 24 hours at a combined sewer outfall, used where neither the operator's overflow reports nor a published rain rule sets an amount
default.cost_rationale: What the default costs. This site's own analysis compared Massachusetts operators' verified reports (July 2022 to October 2026) and Michigan's discharge list (2001 to October 2026) with NOAA radar rainfall. By the operators' own rain figures, overflows that began with less than 0.1 inch of rain were about 3 percent of Massachusetts discharge days and 1 percent of Michigan's; by radar, the 0.1 inch default would have flagged 96 to 97 percent of past overflow days. But on about half of the days with 0.1 inch or more by radar at a Massachusetts operator's outfalls, no overflow was reported that day or in the next two (two days in three for the 12 Michigan operators tested), so where the default applies the caution will often show with no overflow following. In Massachusetts, the operators' own amounts cut those quiet days from 50 to 34 percent while keeping nine overflows in ten. A day with no report is not proof that no overflow happened: some overflows are reported late or not at all.
default.cost_source: MassDEP Sewage Notification Data System, Verified Data Reports, July 2022 to October 2026; Michigan EGLE, MiEnviro CSO/SSO List, 2001 to October 2026; NOAA MRMS radar-only daily rainfall, via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet; analysis by DirtyWaterWatch, November 2026

RI.basis: Rhode Island closes shellfish areas in Narragansett Bay after 0.5 inch of rain
RI.source: Rhode Island DEM shellfish program, rainfall closures

ME.basis: Maine Healthy Beaches issues rainfall advisories after 1 inch or more of rain in 24 hours

NY.basis: New York lets operators issue combined sewer advisories from rainfall data or models; New York City's waterbody advisory model uses a rainfall threshold of 0.1 inch on most of its waters
NY.source: 6 NYCRR 750-2.7(b)(2)(iii); New York City Department of Environmental Protection, Waterbody Advisory System

MD.basis: Maryland's beach program advises avoiding swimming within 48 hours of a heavy rain event, and Anne Arundel County puts its beaches under a no-contact advisory after half an inch of rain. The local half-inch figure is advice for beaches, so we apply our default of 0.1 inch in 24 hours at combined sewer outfalls
MD.source: Maryland Department of the Environment, Healthy Beaches; Anne Arundel County Department of Health, recreational water closings and advisories

DC.basis: District and county agencies recommend not swimming for 48 hours after half an inch of rain, as Anacostia Riverkeeper publishes their advice. The local half-inch figure is advice for beaches, so we apply our default of 0.1 inch in 24 hours at combined sewer outfalls
DC.source: Anacostia Riverkeeper, Swim Guide listings for the District of Columbia

fallback._by_permit_doc: An operator's own published rain trigger for one permit, in the operator's season (months), with its own caution length (tail_hours): it applies before the state's rule, and outside its months the state's rule or the default applies (build/rain_likely.py operator_rule).

_internal_doc: Advisory windows the status computation applies (docs/plan.md section 2). Owner decision 2026-11-02: 72 hours is the site default for the yellow caution, overridable by event type, water kind and water body, each with its rationale, so the rule can be adjusted and explained. Hours count from the reported end of the discharge (ended_at); while a discharge is ongoing it is red. Resolution order for yellow: by_water > by_water_kind > by_event_type > default. Every override must carry a rationale and a source. Public wording (2026-11-02d, from the public-copy review docs/reviews/2026-11-02-copy-review.md): principle, every doc, basis, rationale and *_rationale string and every source is printed on the site exactly as written here (out/rules.json is the site's only copy of the rule text), so they stay in the public voice: no owner, project or file references, citations in source. A rationale that states a number of hours, days or kilometres must match the number beside it (pipeline/tests/test_public_export.py checks). The evidence behind each number is in research/science/report.md; the rain-likely design (per-outfall rainfall thresholds from permittee notices, RIDEM and NYC DEP rules, MRMS radar) is in docs/plan.md section 2 and docs/source-checklist.md. Keys starting with an underscore are internal and are stripped from the public export (out/rules.json).
